correctness.rationale: The admissible symmetric SLEM problem is reduced by convex averaging to two nonnegative transition weights, with exact Walsh-character eigenvalues. The dimension-five and -six optima are proved by positive rational convex dual certificates matching every Fourier mode; d=3,4 reduce to complete bicliques. At every integer dimension at least seven a signed combination of j=1 and j=d eigenvalues gives the sharp lower bound and forces zero short-edge weight, while the Krawtchouk cubic factorization proves the candidate meets every eigenvalue constraint. Group averaging of nonnegative matrices transfers the zero-orbit statement to every unrestricted optimum. The included exact checker confirms the critical identities and finite sample spectra; universal quantifiers follow from algebra, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: Statement-level novelty rests on a sharp non-edge-transitive optimization transition: for the binary graph permitting 1- and 3-coordinate flips, dimensions five and six need a positive 1-flip edge orbit, while from dimension seven every optimal symmetric stochastic matrix assigns all 1-flip edges zero. The detailed optimal rates, small exceptional dimensions, unrestricted edge-deletion consequence, and exact dimension-seven boundary are absent from the inspected relevant sections of the general Boyd–Diaconis–Xiao and Boyd–Diaconis–Parrilo–Xiao source texts. Karlin–Lindqvist–Yao (1993) treats hypercube spectra/majorization, but only its abstract was accessible: the possible implication of an uninspected general theorem remains a specific originality risk, not a conclusion that the paper is noncovering.
residual_risks: The full text of Karlin, Lindqvist and Yao (1993) was not accessible; it could cover or dominate the present hypercube two-orbit minimax despite its spectral-majorization abstract not making this explicit.
Search coverage of specialized finite-cube fastest mixing literature is incomplete; a negative keyword or semantic-search hit list is not proof of novelty.
Published public database records for the closest named alternative objects were compared from index statements rather than full text, so no whole-document noncoverage is asserted for them.

value.rationale: A natural two-range random walk (one- or three-bit flips) has a sharp optimization-driven phase transition: extending the set of allowed edges beyond the ordinary cube paradoxically makes every nearest-neighbor edge universally unused starting at the exact dimension seven. This is a global, all-optimizer structural statement over an infinite family, with two distinct exceptional weight regimes and exact optimal SLEM. It is not just recomputation of a known single-shell graph table; its relevance is the complete characterization of when locally permitted moves become spectrally wasteful. The already-standard complete-biclique base cases are excluded from the substantive novelty claim.
